Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

conservative adjective and noun

in politics

also conservatives, conservatism, traditionalist

modern

M-O s.v. conservative (Egger)

rērum cōnservandārum fautor

noun phrase: fautor, fautōris m.; for a woman, fautrīx

a conservative: one who favours keeping things as they are

A modern description in classical words, built on cōnservāre, to keep, preserve. Traupman gives optimātēs for the conservatives of ancient Rome (p. 178), but the optimātēs were the men who worked through the senate and the leading families, and the populārēs those who worked through the people’s assemblies (Cic. Sest. 96, Lewis & Short s.v. optimās): methods and alliances, not programmes. Neither is a modern conservative or liberal party, and the words are best not used for them.

Other words

  • mōrum trāditōrum fautor — a supporter of traditional ways

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. conservative

    Of a conservative in outlook rather than in party.

  • cōnservātīvus, cōnservātīva, cōnservātīvum — conservative; as a noun, a conservative

    also used · modern · Traupman 178; Traupman 296 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Traupman’s coinage, adjective and noun; no ancient word has this form.

Examples

  • optimātēs, optimātium m. pl.

    the conservatives (in ancient Rome)Traupman 296

See also liberal, party, traditional, opposition.
